claim: Both relevant act families entered into force on 24 December 2024; applying the 24- and 36-month periods in Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 yields working dates of 24 December 2026 and 24 December 2027.

Public bodies must accept wallets where Member States require e-identification for an online service; covered non-small private parties and very large online platforms have separate, narrower duties that depend respectively on strong online-identification authentication or existing platform authentication, and on the user's voluntary request.

Article 5f(2) lists transport, energy, banking, financial services, social security, health, drinking water, postal services, digital infrastructure, education and telecommunications as areas included in the conditional private acceptance rule.
Pre-employment screening is not named in Article 5f(2); a particular screener would need to satisfy the rule's separate legal-or-contractual strong-authentication condition.

A wallet relying party must register where established, declare identity, contacts, intended use and requested data, request no other data, update changes, identify itself and validate credentials; intermediaries are deemed relying parties and may not store transaction-content data.

Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/848 applies from 24 December 2026 and requires national registers, registration policies, public interfaces and access-certificate authorities, while registration certificates are optional; registrars must verify application information against supporting documents or official records and verify entitlements, and parties must update information.

The Dutch Digital Government says the public NL Wallet is still in development and will arrive later because national implementing legislation is being prepared, with public consultation expected near the end of 2026.

The Commission records that Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1731 amended implementing acts on protocols, trust, person-identification data and core wallet functions.
